   guardrail was spuriously tripping because PyTorch's caching allocator
   held ~15GB of reserved-but-unallocated memory between datasets that
   never got flushed. Fix: unconditional (not diagnostic-flag-gated)
   `torch.cuda.empty_cache()` once per dataset boundary in the outer batch
   loop — safe because it's not inside a hot per-pair loop (unlike the
   #49 stall cause, which stays opt-in-only). `submodules/ASP` commit
   `3577bcf`.

## Needs Harbinger's call (do not resolve unilaterally)

Surfaced by the #31 fork, both are genuine tensions between a locked
decision and empirical findings, not bugs:

1. **A locked M2 exit criterion may be infeasible as specified.** Harbinger
   locked "Safe ASP must be discriminating — pick Raw ASP on at least one
   known-good red-set case AND SCANS on every known catastrophe; always-
   SCANS is not M2 success." A full threshold sweep across all three
   existing gates (SeamVis/Composite/Ghost) found **zero** `(floor, ratio)`
   combinations on the current corpus that satisfy this simultaneously —
   this reconfirms Grok's earlier 2026-08-17 finding, not a new problem.
   The existing gates structurally can't do it; it needs a genuinely new
   structural signal, not a tuning pass. Someone needs to tell Harbinger
   this and get a decision: relax the criterion, invest in a new signal
   (open research, no clear path yet), or something else.
2. **CompositeGate is close to dead weight.** Its `sb` component is
   demoted (inverse-correlated with human judgment); `sc` has no
   significant signal on this corpus (1 historic fire, not significant).
   Grok recommended a redesign/retirement; pending Harbinger's sign-off.

Full detail in `submodules/ASP/docs/moon/asp_change_roadmap_2026q3.md` §5
M2 section and the bus posts around 18:00-18:10 today.

## Environment note (new this session)

`submodules/ASP`'s git remotes include ~9 entries named `agentN`/`agentN_M`
pointing at local filesystem paths under
`~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/brain/.../worktrees/subagent-*` — leftover
config from Gemini's own Antigravity subagent worktree tooling, not
something you created or need to clean up. Harmless, just don't be
surprised by them in `git remote -v`; `origin` (GitHub) is still the
correct push target.
